column1: Please note:  This datalayer is DRAFT and only shows sewer areas for a select number of systems in Massachusetts – it is a subset of a larger datalayer of all publicly owned and large to medium sewer systems in MA.  All Sewer Service Area delineations are estimates for broad planning purposes and should only be used as a guide.  The data is not appropriate for site specific analysis.  Properties within a sewer service area may not necessarily be served by the system – please contact the relevant Wastewater System or MassDEP for more information.

The MassDEP Estimated Selected Sewer Service Areas datalayer is currently under development and may not be complete, may contain errors, omissions and other inaccuracies; and is subject to change for any reason - it has not yet been approved or made available to the general public.   The datalayer may include information about the sources and years the service areas are based on.  Service areas described in the draft Document are approximate and should not be used for site specific determinations of water service. All Sewer Water Service Area delineations are estimates for broad planning purposes and should only be used as a guide.  Properties within a sewer service area may not necessarily be served by the system.

In 2017, as part of its Critical Infrastructure Mapping Project, the MassDEP Water Utility Resilience Program (WURP) https://www.mass.gov/guides/water-utility-resilience-program began an initiative to uniformly map sewer and drinking water service areas throughout Massachusetts using information collected from various sources and confirmed by the systems and municipalities involved (see https://www.mass.gov/guides/water-utility-resilience-program#-critical-infrastructure-gis-mapping-initiative- for more information). Along with confirming existing service area information, the project collected and verified estimated service area delineations for systems and continues to improve the information contained in the datalayers.

The mapped sewer service areas and municipal percent served by sewer information are based on publicly owned treatment systems or medium to large sewer districts only and does not include privately owned treatment systems with groundwater discharges - even those that have been permitted by DEP are generally not included in the calculation of percent served by sewer.

MassDEP has not received information or confirmation from systems for all sewered areas in the state  but will continue to collect this information.   Some service areas included in this datalayer have not been verified by the sewer system or the municipality involved but since those areas are based on information published online by the municipality or the system or in a publicly available report, they have been included in the estimated sewer areas datalayer.

Wastewater treatment plants in Massachusetts are permitted either through the NPDES surface water discharge permit program or the MassDEP Groundwater discharge permit program (see https://www.mass.gov/wastewater for more information). These permitted discharges were used in combination with the information from the individual municipalities they serve as a basis for identifying the delineated service areas as unique entities. The Sewer Service Area datalayer contains polygons that represent the service area of a particular wastewater system within a particular municipality.  Some wastewater systems serve more than one municipality – these systems are represented by separate polygons for each municipality that they serve.  Some towns are served by more than one wastewater system – these are also shown as separate polygons.
